cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine review October's receivables for HANGS Construction.
Receivables are the money customers owe. First it ties the open invoices and retainage to the ledger.
Next it applies October's customer payments to their invoices.
Then retainage: the part of each bill a customer holds back until the job is done.
It recomputes retainage on six jobs and checks the latest pay application.
An agreed credit was never issued.
One customer is past ninety days, owing about $48,000.
Three reminder letters are drafted but not sent, and the allowance for bad debts is raised to policy.
All done. Corrected receivables are about $451,000, with four entries proposed and five exceptions. Nothing was posted or sent; the controller approves every entry and letter.
Jumping to the results. A person still reviews every item before anything is posted, paid or sent.
